description.text: Bio-Techne and its subsidiaries, collectively doing business as Bio-Techne Corporation (“Bio-Techne”, “we”, “our”, “us” or the “Company”), develop, manufacture and sell life science reagents, instruments and services for the research, diagnostics and bioprocessing markets worldwide. Our broad product portfolio and application expertise enables scientific investigations into biological processes and molecular diagnostics, revealing the nature, diagnosis, etiology and progression of specific diseases. Our products aid in drug discovery efforts and provide the means for accurate clinical tests and diagnoses. We manage the business in two operating segments – our Protein Sciences segment and our Diagnostics and Spatial Biology segment. Our Protein Sciences segment is a leading developer and manufacturer of high-quality biological reagents used in all aspects of life science research, diagnostics and cell and gene therapy. This segment also includes proteomic analytical tools, both manual and automated, that offer researchers and pharmaceutical manufacturers efficient and streamlined options for protein analysis, automated western blot, and multiplexed ELISA workflows.

about.description_short: Bio-Techne Corporation (NASDAQ: TECH) is a global life sciences company headquartered in Minnesota, celebrating 50 years of empowering scientific and diagnostic communities to reach better answers. The company provides high-quality reagents, analytical instruments, and precision diagnostics. Its portfolio is organized into three customer-focused brands: R&D Systems, Bio-Techne Spatial, and Bio-Techne Diagnostics, reflecting the scientific journey from discovery to translational research to clinical decision-making. Bio-Techne operates in 34 locations worldwide and employs more than 3,000 people. In fiscal year 2025, the company generated over $1.2 billion in net sales. Its more than 500,000 products are used globally by academic researchers, biopharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, and clinical diagnostic laboratories.

analysis_md:
# TECH — Bio-Techne Corporation
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-18. Price $72.57 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap est. $11.394B — in scope under $40B. **The headline fact about this stock is not in the DCF: on June 25, 2026 Bio-Techne agreed to be acquired by Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany for $73.00/share in cash (enterprise value ~$11.3B). The $72.57 price is the deal price minus a ~0.6% merger spread. This analysis scores the standalone business — i.e. the break value if the deal fails — and on that basis it is a Tier D by a wide margin.**

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or segments.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Life-sciences tools: proteins, antibodies and immunoassays (R&D Systems, Novus, Tocris), protein-analysis instruments and consumables (ProteinSimple), and spatial biology / molecular diagnostics (RNAscope, Lunaphore COMET). Two segments (segments.json, FY2026): Protein Sciences $874,620,000 (72.0% of revenue, +0.5% YoY) and Diagnostics and Spatial Biology $336,365,000 (27.7%, −2.9% YoY). Q4 FY2026 (company release): net sales $321.2M, +1% reported / +3% organic, adjusted EPS $0.52 vs $0.53 a year ago; full-year adjusted EPS $1.93 vs $1.92.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K, period ended 2026-06-30):** operating cash flow $292,073,000; capex $28,850,000; SBC $41,365,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $221,858,000 = $1.41/share** (OCF − capex − SBC).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $204,647,000 — same ballpark, which raises confidence in the base.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. OE/share path: FY2022 $1.45, FY2023 $1.09, FY2024 $1.23, FY2025 $1.35, FY2026 $1.41 — a dip in FY2023 and a slow rebuild since, not a growth ramp.
- **Base used = $1.35/share, the median of the last 3 fiscal years** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The FY ended 3.6 months ago, no STALE_FY flag, and the three base years are tightly clustered ($1.23 / $1.35 / $1.41), so the median is the right base — no TTM override needed (TTM through FY2026 is the fiscal year itself; fundamentals.json TTM OE/share is $1.41, the latest-FY figure).
- Balance sheet: net debt −$64,712,000 — i.e. net cash (debt $200,000,000 vs cash $264,712,000 on the engine's basis; lease liabilities of $89,087,000 sit outside that figure). Net debt is −0.31x normalized OE. No leverage story either way.
- History caveat: share counts before FY2021 in financials_history.csv are on the pre-split basis (the 4-for-1 split effective 2022-11-01 was restated into later filings only from FY2021), so OE/share of ~$3.0–3.2 printed for FY2017–20 is not comparable to today's ~$1.4. Nothing in the base or the 2-yr OE/share CAGR touches those years; revenue CAGRs are on absolute revenue and are unaffected.
- Payout: dividend $0.32/share (flat), small buybacks shrinking the count ~1.0%/yr (share_cagr −1.01%), already credited in the growth blend via the +1.01pp adjustment to the revenue components.

## Moat: 7/10 — strong, but no longer compounding like one
Justification: R&D Systems is the reference standard for cytokines/growth factors — catalog products are cited by number in the scientific literature, and a failed assay costs a lab weeks, so reproducibility trust beats small price differences; that shows up as 65–68% gross margins held every year through the 2023–26 tools downturn. Instrument placements (ProteinSimple, COMET) pull proprietary consumables, and GMP-grade reagents are qualified into cell-therapy manufacturing processes where switching means re-validation. Merck KGaA paying $73 cash / ~$11.3B EV for the whole franchise is a market test that a sophisticated strategic buyer sees the same durability.
- FOR: Reference-standard citation lock-in for R&D Systems proteins/antibodies — displacement would take a competitor decades of parallel citation history; gross margin 68.0% / 68.4% / 67.7% / 66.4% / 64.8% / 65.8% (FY2021–26, fundamentals.json) — pricing power held through a downcycle; instrument + proprietary consumable pull-through (ProteinSimple, Lunaphore COMET, RNAscope as the spatial sensitivity standard); regulated GMP reagent positions embedded in customers' validated manufacturing workflows; net-cash balance sheet.
- AGAINST: Subscale against Thermo Fisher and Danaher, who can bundle across the whole lab wallet; revenue essentially flat for three years (FY2023 $1,136,702,000 → FY2026 $1,215,039,000) — the moat defends share and margin, it is not currently producing growth; ROIC (roic_proxy, fundamentals.json) down from 14.5% (FY2022) and 13.1% (FY2021) to 11.8% / 8.4% / 3.6% / 9.3% (FY2023–26) — the FY2025 print is depressed by the non-cash held-for-sale impairment and litigation/arbitration charges that hit operating income directly, but FY2024 and FY2026 also sit below the earlier level; Diagnostics and Spatial Biology is the weaker, lower-margin segment and shrank −2.9% in FY2026; demand rides the biotech funding cycle (the 2023–24 funding winter is what flattened revenue); balance sheet carries a large acquired goodwill/intangible base from the roll-up years.
- ROIC note (required for a 7): measured ROIC has NOT stayed well above the cost of capital through the recent cycle — it slid from the low-to-mid teens to high single digits. The 7 rests on the written reasons the recent series understates the franchise: FY2025's 3.6% is a one-off year (impairment + arbitration/litigation in operating income), the denominator carries the full acquired-intangible/goodwill stack from acquisitions whose consumable pull-through is still ramping, gross margins never broke, and a strategic acquirer just validated the franchise at $73 cash. It is capped at 7, not 8, because the ROIC downtrend and the three flat revenue years are real erosion signals, not noise.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — 5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine's blended start is 4.87% (components: revenue CAGR 5y 5.47%, 3y 2.25%, latest YoY −0.38%, OE/share CAGR 2y 7.10%; revenue components adjusted +1.01pp for the shrinking share count). Against actual prints — FY2026 revenue −0.4%, Q4 FY2026 organic +3%, FY2025 revenue +5.2% — the base start sits ABOVE the latest fiscal-year print. Reason for keeping it: the blend is anchored on the 5-yr revenue CAGR and the 7.10% OE/share CAGR, Q4 organic growth already inflected back to +3%, and ~5% is this franchise's through-cycle rate (FY2017–22 revenue roughly doubled). The bear start of −0.13% is the one that matches the current flat print, and it carries 25%. Bull (9.87%) and super-bull (16.87%) starts are scenario tails — a biotech-funding boom plus a spatial/GMP ramp — not forecasts; they are kept at the standard offsets precisely so the table shows that even those tails do not rescue the tier at $72.57. Probabilities and OE multipliers are the defaults 10/25/30/25/10 and 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 — no company-specific reason to skew them, and no plausible skew changes the verdict. Price $72.57.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −7.13% | 0.75 | Funding winter returns; tools budgets cut; margins give back | $5.30 | 3.24% |
| Bear | 25% | −0.13% | 0.90 | The current flat-revenue regime persists | $8.81 | 3.94% |
| Base | 30% | 4.87% | 1.00 | Through-cycle mid-single-digit growth resumes | $12.38 | 4.72% |
| Bull | 25% | 9.87% | 1.10 | Biotech funding recovery + spatial/GMP ramp | $17.27 | 5.78% |
| Super bull | 10% | 16.87% | 1.25 | Category-leader re-acceleration for a decade | $27.37 | 7.87% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $13.50 (−81.4% vs price), IV@12% $18.09, IV@10% $23.23, weighted IRR 5.01%, base-case IRR 4.72%**
- **Tier by numbers: D — and bear and bull are both D too; every single scenario is Tier D.** Diagnostics: OE yield 1.86%, terminal value 19.7% of IV@15%, scenario spread 5.17x, net debt −0.31x normalized OE, 3.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices: clears 15% only at or below **$13.50**, 20% at $9.41, 25% at $7.18.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs OCF differ by >40% in 2024, 2025): resolved — structural plus one-offs, and it does not touch the base. Bio-Techne's OCF structurally exceeds net income because OCF adds back D&A ($111,711,000 in FY2024; $109,903,000 in FY2025, including heavy acquired-intangible amortization) and SBC ($38,042,000 / $40,833,000) while capex runs far smaller ($62,877,000 / $31,006,000). FY2025 widened the gap (NI $73,400,000 vs OCF $287,556,000) with non-cash / one-off charges that hit net income but not operating cash: an impairment of assets held for sale of $80,503,000 for the full year (the Exosome Diagnostics divestiture; $84.2M was the Q4 charge as reported at the time), certain litigation charges of $41,827,000 (arbitration-related, per the FY2025 release reconciliation), and restructuring of $28,231,000 — cutting FY2025 GAAP operating income to $102,255,000 (8.4% margin) against an adjusted operating margin of 31.6%. FY2026 confirms the one-off read: with the impairment gone, net income recovered to $181,862,000 and operating income to $251,890,000 while OCF was essentially flat at $292,073,000. The conservative OE used throughout is OCF-based and subtracts SBC and capex in full, so the divergence inflates nothing.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (base OE yield 1.86%): real and decisive. At $72.57 the buyer gets $1.35/share of owner's earnings — the price capitalizes the franchise's strategic/scarcity value (and, concretely, a signed cash takeover), not its current cash generation. The standalone tier therefore rests almost entirely on growth and duration, which is exactly why it is sized to the conservative end and why confidence is not high.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 5.17x super-bear IV): real, but here it cuts against the stock, not for it — even the super-bull IV@15% of $27.37 sits 62% below the price. The spread reflects the low base yield (small base, long duration), not disagreement about the business. Confidence capped at medium.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The $73.00 Merck KGaA cash deal is the security now. If it closes, holders receive $73.00 — a +0.6% spread over $72.57, an arbitrage return whose annualized value depends entirely on closing timing and completion risk, neither of which this DCF measures. The company has stopped holding earnings calls in light of the transaction.
- What this DCF actually measures is the break value: if the deal fails, the standalone weighted IV@15% is $13.50 and even the super-bull path only reaches $27.37. That is the honest downside map — a break would not be a 10–20% correction, it would be a repricing toward a low-teens handle unless another bidder appeared. Merck is paying roughly 5.4x the standalone weighted IV@15% because it is buying strategic position, synergies and a scarce reference-standard franchise, not a 15%-hurdle cash stream.
- Standalone quality is genuinely good — net cash, ~66% gross margins, OE positive 5/5 years, dividend paid — but quality is not the question at this price; the OE yield is 1.86% after three flat revenue years and a ROIC slide. As a fundamentals investment TECH stopped clearing any hurdle long before $72.57; it cleared 15% only under $13.50.
- Method range: narrow for once. Latest-FY base ($1.41) instead of the median ($1.35), or the preliminary moat-5 run, move the weighted IV@15% only within roughly $13–14 and the weighted IRR within ~4.9–5.0% — every defensible variant is a deep Tier D. The tier does not rest on an override; there are no overrides in this run.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 5.01% standalone; every scenario, bear to super bull, is individually Tier D)
- Confidence: **Medium** (clean filings, no data gaps, tightly clustered base years; capped by the wide scenario spread and the fact that the traded price is set by a pending merger, not by the fundamentals scored here)
- One-liner: High-quality life-sciences tools franchise, moat 7/10, but standalone owner's-earnings value is ~$13.50 vs the $72.57 price — the price is Merck KGaA's pending $73 cash takeover, not fundamentals; Tier D standalone (5.0% weighted IRR), clears 15% only below $13.50, and a deal break leaves the whole DCF range far below the price.
